name: University of Hull

settingEvidence.evidence: explore our beautiful single-site campus and state-of-the-art facilities

fees.text: £10,050 per year for UK students on Hull's Business School course pages (Hull says to use 2027-28 information as a guide because fees for 2028 entry aren't confirmed). Hull's main fees page and its PPE course page still say £9,790. Those course pages also list £1,505 for a year abroad, £2,010 for a year in industry and £5,760 for a foundation year.

source.evidence: For UK students, our standard course fee is £10,050 per year.

livingCosts.text: University halls cost about £99 to £315 a week on 43 or 51 week contracts (2026/27 prices): Taylor Court £99 to £180, Westfield Court £135 to £315.

source.evidence: On-campus, en-suite accommodation starting from £99 a week.

openDays.text: Next undergraduate open day: Saturday 28 November 2026 on campus (no later dates listed yet). Campus visits can be booked all year round, and Hull offers an Open Day travel grant of up to £100 if you travel more than 40 miles.

source.evidence: Saturday 28 November 2026

contextual.summary: If you meet two or more of Hull's criteria you can get a contextual offer of 96 UCAS points, applied automatically from your UCAS application.
contextual.typicalReduction: A contextual offer is 96 UCAS points, which Hull says is lower than its standard entry requirements (on the economics and business courses recorded here the typical offer is 96 to 112 points, so it equals the bottom of that range).

criteria.detail: You live in an area with a low number of young people progressing to higher education (Hull's summary page: an area with historically low progression to higher education or an area of high relative deprivation). Hull doesn't name the measure or quintiles.
You are care experienced (have spent time in local authority care).
You are from a military family.
You are a refugee or asylum seeker.
You are, or have been, eligible for free school meals.
You are the first person in your family to attend higher education (neither parent or guardian attended university).
You are a member of the Gypsy, Traveller, Roma, Showmen or Boater communities.
You are estranged from your family.
You have other relevant circumstances that aren't listed.

contextual.rulesText: You may qualify for a contextual offer if you meet two or more of the listed criteria. If you qualify, Hull applies the offer automatically from your UCAS application (admissions staff assess your circumstances and assign qualifying points). Offers can be made to home and international applicants completing UK qualifications that carry UCAS tariff points. Not available for Foundation Year entry or programmes with mandatory placements or capped student numbers; the listed exclusions are BA British Politics & Legislative Studies, LLB Law & Legislative Studies, BA Primary Teaching with Foundation Year and health programmes such as nursing and midwifery.

source.evidence: You may be eligible for a contextual offer if you meet two or more of our criteria.

programmes.name: Taster Days
programmes.summary: Free day on campus for post-16 students with a campus tour, a talk or workshop, a chance to meet current students and lecturers, and a subject masterclass led by academics.
programmes.whoCanApply: Post-16 students, typically in Year 12, Year 13 or equivalent. Hull welcomes group bookings from schools and colleges across the UK; the page doesn't say whether individual students can book.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Open to post-16 students (typically Year 12, Year 13 or equivalent); organised as group bookings by schools and colleges.
benefits: Guided campus tour and a chance to meet current students and lecturers
Subject masterclass led by academic staff
A chance to ask questions before applying
programmes.subjects: Subject masterclasses (subjects vary); not specific to Economics

runs.text: Dates are arranged with the school or college; no fixed dates published

programmes.infoNote: Current Hull page (checked 2026-10-21) describes the standing offer for schools and colleges; no dates are published.

source.evidence: Our free taster days give post-16 students the chance to visit our campus and experience university life first-hand.

notConfirmed: dates and how to book are not published on the page; it describes group bookings by schools and colleges
